l.i: Honorii Divalia constituta, quæ Theodosianum corpus
ostendit, præter religionem posse cognoscere. Si
ambo ejusdem officii litigatores nolint, vel alterutèr[?], agant
publicis legibus & jure communi. Sin verò petitor Laicus,
seu in civili, seu in criminali causa cujuslibet
loci Clericum adversarium suum, si ita magis eligat, per
authoritatem legitimam in publico judicio respondere
compellat. Quam formam etiam circa Episcoporum personam
observari oportere censemus. Ut si in hujusmodi
injuriarum dirigi necesse fuerit, per procuratorem solenniter
ordinatum apud Judicem publicum inter leges &
jura confligant. Vid. Cod. Theod. Novell. Valentia. L.

main_text.l: §. 3. Confilium autem, ex quo istiusmodi studia
profluxerunt, nullum aliud fuit, quam ut se contra
potestatem mundanam munirent, seque Principum
jurisdictioni eximerent, à quibus se haud raro graviora passos
fuisse erant memores: ne itaque in posterum
habeant, quod sibi ab iis metuant, omni studio & cona-
tu se ex istâ manu mali eximere conabantur. Quod
factum à sede Romanâ, duos sibi gladios vendicante,
temporalem & spiritualem: ex eodem principio

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Doubtful readings: "alterutèr" (the last letters are unclear) and "atrociun" (the final letter is unclear, possibly atrocium). The last line is cut off after "L.", so the text stops there. The top line "2. Tit. 12." is treated as a running head. The leading „ marks at the start of several lines are printed quotation continuation marks and are kept as printed. The text ends with the hyphenated word "man-", which runs on in the part of the page that is not shown. A small bullet in the left margin beside "potestatem" is a printed mark, not text, and is not transcribed.
